prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1059; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received on a low-speed head-on collision. Insured vehicle and other vehicle both sustained front-end damage. Claimant reports back strain and is now represented by counsel. Letter of representation received and logged. All further contact to be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office to confirm representation scope. Requested medical authorization forms and prior treatment history for the lumbar region. Attorney indicated a demand package will follow once treatment concludes. Noted that no recorded statement will be taken from the claimant directly.

Entry 3: Reviewed police report. Responding officer documented minimal intrusion into either cabin and no airbag deployment. Both drivers reported speeds under moderate range at impact. Photos from the scene show bumper and hood deformation consistent with a low-energy impact. Liability assessment in progress.

Entry 4: Received initial treatment records from claimant's provider. Diagnosis listed as acute lumbar strain with conservative care recommended, including physical therapy and short-term medication. No imaging ordered at this stage. Forwarded records to the medical review unit for evaluation of reasonableness and relatedness.

Entry 5: Attorney's office confirmed claimant is continuing physical therapy and expects an updated report in the coming weeks. Reserve reviewed and maintained at current level pending medical review outcome. Follow-up diary set for the next status check. File remains open and under active handling.
